category: per-address static ISP proxy (native residential and home-broadband broadcast) with a residential GB product
tier: Static ISP, per IP, 7, 30 or 90 days

free_tier.stated: No free tier is stated on the pages read. Static ISP is sold per IP: Residential Native from $3.8/IP (United States) to $10.0/IP (Thailand, Dubai $8.0/IP), and Home broadband broadcast from $3.0/IP (Germany). Dynamic residential traffic is "As Low as $0.58/GB" and does not expire.
free_tier.notes: The page lists validity columns 7 day, 30 day and 90 day and up to two prices per location, but the read does not keep the column of each price, so the term that a printed price buys is unverified.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic pack, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not stored bytes. Lease terms are 7, 30 and 90 days.
retention.notes: days is null because no bytes are stored.

egress.terms: Static ISP: Unlimited Traffic, no charge for unused IPs; the unit sold is an address for a term.
egress.free_allowance: unlimited for the static ISP product

interface_detail: Proxy endpoints with sub-accounts, managed through a control panel or an API (documentation at help.cliproxy.com); the residential product supports fixed and rotating sessions.
tooling: Any client that speaks SOCKS5 or an HTTP proxy, reached from a Worker through a relay that dials SOCKS5. An API with language samples for C/C++, Go, Node.js, PHP, Java and Python is named on the vendor page.
chaining: The upstream sees the leased address. The page separates Residential Native from Home broadband broadcast, the latter a lower price class; no delivered address was seen, so the registration class is unverified.

limits.value: one dedicated address per unit, unlimited traffic, terms of 7, 30 and 90 days
none for the static ISP product; dynamic residential traffic is sold by the GB and never expires

binding_note: Traffic is unlimited; the single address and its registration class bind, and the page itself prices the broadcast class lower than the native one.

identity_cost.detail: No phone, card or ID document is asked on that page; a card may be asked at checkout, which was not read.

reliability_note: The vendor states 99% success and 99% uptime; no throughput, ban or replacement measurement was made.
confidence_note: Prices and labels read from vendor pages on 2026-11-03; no IP was bought and no address was published, so the delivered class is unmeasured.
price_per_tb_month: not applicable: an address, not a byte; from USD 3.0 per IP (home-broadband broadcast, Germany) and USD 3.8 per IP (Residential Native, United States)
notes: Named on the Chinese-language forum source as a static-residential lead; the forum is the lead and the evidence is the vendor page.

extras.rung_note: Native versus broadcast is the registration-class claim; nothing was looked up.

evidence.proved: The static ISP product is labelled Native Residential IP.
The static ISP product states unlimited traffic.
The static ISP terms are 7, 30 and 90 days.
The United States Residential Native price points are $3.8 and $5.0 per IP.
Home broadband broadcast Germany is $3.0 per IP.
Dynamic residential traffic starts at $0.58 per GB.
The sign-up page takes an email address, a password and an optional invitation code.
